rank_math_desc: 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse with an acclimatisation day at Shipton Camp before Point Lenana at sunrise. Porters and park fees included.
post_content: This 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse climbs the Sirimon route, adds an acclimatisation day at Shipton Camp, summits Point Lenana at sunrise and descends the Chogoria route.
overview:
This 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse climbs the Sirimon route via Judmaier Camp (3,300 m), spends two nights at Shipton Camp (4,200 m) with an acclimatisation day, reaches Point Lenana (4,985 m) at sunrise on day 4 and descends the Chogoria route to Nairobi. Price on request; it suits fit first-time Mount Kenya trekkers who want a better chance of summiting.

The trek is graded Expert on the page, with porters, a guide and full board in camps and bandas. The extra day at Shipton Camp is what sets it apart from our four-day version. You need your own sleeping bag and climbing gear, which are not included.

Why choose a 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse?

The Sirimon to Chogoria traverse pairs the gradual, drier northern approach with the dramatic eastern descent past the Gorges Valley, so you see two sides of Mount Kenya. The acclimatisation day at 4,200 m gives your body time to adjust before the 3:00 a.m. summit start, which makes the climb more comfortable and the summit more likely.

  • First time at altitude: a rest and acclimatisation walk at Shipton Camp before summit day.
  • Scenery: Mackinder's Valley, the Hausburg tarns and the Gorges Valley.
  • Kilimanjaro training: a high-altitude trek above 4,900 m that is shorter than a Kilimanjaro climb.

What to expect on the 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse

Day 1 leaves Nairobi at 8:00 a.m. for about four hours to Nanyuki for lunch, then an hour to Sirimon Gate (2,440 m) and a walk of 3 to 4 hours through forest and heathland to Judmaier Camp (3,300 m). Day 2 crosses the Ontulili River and Liki North and climbs Mackinder's Valley, with views of the main peaks, to Shipton Camp (4,200 m). Day 3 is an acclimatisation day of about 6 hours, walking to Kami Hut and the Hausburg and Nanyuki tarns before returning to Shipton Camp.

Day 4 starts at 3:00 a.m. with a steep climb through the cliff band to Point Lenana by about 6:30 a.m. for sunrise. You descend 6 km to Mintos Hut for breakfast, then about 20 km down the Chogoria route to Mount Meru Bandas (2,950 m), 11 to 12 hours and 32 km in total. On day 5 you walk down through moorland and giant heather to the forest clearing, ride a 4x4 for 21 km to Chogoria and arrive back in Nairobi by late afternoon or early evening.

Why does an acclimatisation day matter on Mount Kenya?

Mount Kenya rises quickly from the road head, and altitude sickness is the main reason trekkers turn back before Point Lenana. A day spent walking higher and sleeping again at 4,200 m helps your body adjust before the summit push. If you are short on time and already used to altitude, the 4 Days Mt Kenya Sirimon-Chogoria Route skips this day. Thinking about Kilimanjaro next? Our Kilimanjaro routes guide compares the options, and the Kenya packing list covers warm layers.

What is included in this Mount Kenya climb?

The price includes porterage, the rescue fee, non-resident park fees, camping equipment, a professional guide, all transport and the round-trip transfer, meals as listed in the day-by-day plan, drinking water every day, all activities and accommodation in the itinerary, and all taxes and VAT.

Not included are climbing gear, a sleeping bag, bath towels, international flights, extra nights before or after the trek, travel insurance, visa fees, souvenirs and any government increase in taxes or park fees. Tips are extra, with a guideline of about USD 10 per person per day; our guide to tipping in Kenya explains how to tip a Mount Kenya crew.

faq.q: Which route does the 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse follow?
faq.a: The 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse goes up the Sirimon route and down the Chogoria route. You sleep at Judmaier Camp, spend two nights at Shipton Camp with an acclimatisation walk to the Hausburg tarns, reach Point Lenana at sunrise on day 4, then descend to Mount Meru Bandas and walk out to Chogoria on day 5.

faq.q: How high do you climb on the 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse?
faq.a: The highest point on the 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse is Point Lenana at 4,985 m. You sleep at 3,300 m and then two nights at 4,200 m, and the acclimatisation day in between helps your body adjust. Altitude symptoms are still possible, so walk slowly, drink plenty of water and tell your guide early.

faq.q: How fit do I need to be for the 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse?
faq.a: The 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse is graded Expert on the page. No climbing skills are needed, but summit day is 11 to 12 hours and about 32 km, starting at 3:00 a.m. Regular long hill walks for six to eight weeks are the best preparation, and tell us the ages of any younger trekkers so we can advise.

faq.q: When is the best time for the 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse?
faq.a: The best time for the 5 day Mount Kenya Sirimon Chogoria traverse is in the drier months, usually January to February and July to October, when trails are firmer and sunrise views from Point Lenana are clearer. The rains around April to May and November make the forest sections muddy, so ask us before booking in those months.
